chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'aba ibn Maymun, from the one who narrated it, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

Indeed, Allah is Kind (Rafiq), He loves kindness, and from His kindness to you is the easing of your grudges and the antagonism of your hearts. And indeed, He intends to turn the servant away from a matter, so He leaves it upon him until He turns it away by the Abrogating (Nasikh), disliking the heaviness of the truth upon him.

key_terms.النَّاسِخِ: The Abrogating, The One who removes/turns away

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when Allah is described as 'Kind' in this hadith and how does He ease our hearts?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith elucidates the divine attribute of Rifq (gentleness) as the mechanism for dissolving interpersonal animosity, linking spiritual tranquility to social harmony. Scholars interpret the 'turning away' (tahwil) not as abandonment, but as a merciful delay or redirection to prevent the burden of truth from becoming overwhelming, utilizing the Nasikh (abrogator/transformer) to ease the soul's transition. This reflects the Shia emphasis on Allah’s pedagogical patience, where divine gentleness serves as both a social remedy and a spiritual safeguard.
